latin: Non est credendum in doctrina Platonis animam quicquam intelligere per inspectionem ad ideas, nisi cum peruenit ad illum statum qui est supremus gradus contemplatiuae perfectionis.
translation: It must not be believed that, on Plato's teaching, the soul understands anything by looking directly to the ideas, except when it has arrived at that state which is the highest grade of contemplative perfection.
